description: Curated functional-group SMARTS library for Hey Inky molecule cards. RDKit substructure matching decides every highlight. `smarts` lists alternative patterns (matches are unioned). `short` is the on-structure label (defaults to `name`). `core` lists the SMARTS atom positions that are highlighted (default: all). A match of group B is dropped when B appears in another group's `supersedes` and B's core atoms are a subset of that group's matched atoms (e.g. a lactone hides the ester it is made of). Order is display order.

groups.name: Carboxylic acid
groups.description: C(=O)OH — acidic proton; loses H⁺ to form a carboxylate.

groups.name: Anhydride
groups.description: Two acyl groups sharing one oxygen — a reactive acylating agent.

groups.name: Acyl halide
groups.description: C(=O)X — the most reactive carboxylic-acid derivative.

groups.name: Lactone
groups.description: A cyclic ester: the ester C–O bond is part of a ring.

groups.name: Ester
groups.description: C(=O)O–R — made from an acid and an alcohol; hydrolyzes back to them.

groups.name: Lactam
groups.description: A cyclic amide: the amide C–N bond is part of a ring.

groups.name: Primary amide
groups.description: C(=O)NH₂ — planar, resonance-stabilized C–N bond.

groups.name: Secondary amide
groups.description: C(=O)NH–R — the peptide bond in proteins.

groups.name: Tertiary amide
groups.description: C(=O)NR₂ — an amide nitrogen with no N–H.

groups.name: Aldehyde
groups.description: CHO at the end of a chain — easily oxidized to a carboxylic acid.

groups.name: Ketone
groups.description: C=O flanked by two carbons — polar, accepts H-bonds.

groups.name: Nitrile
groups.description: C≡N — linear; hydrolyzes to an amide, then an acid.

groups.name: Nitro
groups.description: NO₂ — strongly electron-withdrawing.

groups.name: Imine
groups.description: C=N — a Schiff base; forms from a carbonyl and an amine.

groups.name: Primary amine
groups.description: R–NH₂ — basic; a lone pair that accepts a proton.

groups.name: Secondary amine
groups.description: R₂NH — basic nitrogen bonded to two carbons.

groups.name: Tertiary amine
groups.description: R₃N — basic nitrogen with no N–H.

groups.name: Hemiacetal
groups.description: One carbon bearing both –OH and –OR — the ring form of sugars.

groups.name: Acetal
groups.description: One carbon bearing two –OR groups — a protected carbonyl; glycosidic bonds.

groups.name: Epoxide
groups.description: A strained three-membered C–O–C ring — opens readily.

groups.name: Phenol
groups.description: –OH on an aromatic ring — more acidic than an alcohol.

groups.name: Primary alcohol
groups.description: –OH on a carbon bonded to at most one other carbon.

groups.name: Secondary alcohol
groups.description: –OH on a carbon bonded to two other carbons.

groups.name: Tertiary alcohol
groups.description: –OH on a carbon bonded to three other carbons.

groups.name: Ether
groups.description: C–O–C — fairly unreactive; H-bond acceptor only.

groups.name: Thiol
groups.description: R–SH — the sulfur analog of an alcohol; forms disulfides.

groups.name: Sulfide
groups.description: C–S–C — a thioether; the sulfur analog of an ether.

groups.name: Sulfonamide
groups.description: S(=O)₂N — the core of sulfa antibiotics.

groups.name: Alkyl halide
groups.description: Halogen on an sp³ carbon — undergoes SN1/SN2 and elimination.

groups.name: Aryl halide
groups.description: Halogen on an aromatic ring — resists SN1/SN2.

groups.name: Alkene
groups.description: C=C — a π bond that undergoes addition reactions.

groups.name: Alkyne
groups.description: C≡C — two π bonds; linear sp carbons.

groups.name: Aromatic ring
groups.description: A flat ring with 4n+2 delocalized π electrons — unusually stable.
